messages:
Alex: Quick sync — we need to finalize router fallback specs for multi-region + customer-tier. Hit a tokenizer parity bug when falling back from `redwood/lg-quant` -> `redwood/lg-8bit` in eu-west. Noticed broken token counts and truncated tool payloads. :eyes:
Maria: Can you paste the minimal repro or the trace? Tokenization issues are usually either special tokens or different tokenizer versions.
Sam: FWIW I saw a related failure where function/tool-calling stopped working because the fallback model expected different function arg quoting. End-to-end calls returned 400s.
Jen: Important: Dedicated customers have strict quota accounting and SLAs. If fallback changes tokenization we must keep quota semantics stable (or clearly surface extra usage). Otherwise billing disputes incoming.
Alex: Thoughts: expand the compat matrix to include these columns: `tokenizer_id`, `tokenizer_hash`, `effective_context_len`, `tool_calling_schema_version`, `kv_cache_compat`, `fallback_safety_flag`. Also add a machine-readable hash so router can quickly check compatibility.
Maria: Agreed. Example quick matrix row format (proto-ish) — we should store it in the compat service: ```
- model: redwood/lg-quant
  tokenizer_id: lg-token-v2
  tokenizer_hash: 9f8a
  effective_context_len: 8192
  tool_calling_schema_version: 2
  kv_cache_compat: true
  fallback_safety_flag: strict
```
Sam: Router policy needs to use the safety flag. If `strict` then only models with exact `tool_calling_schema_version` match are allowed. If `relaxed` we can fallback but emit telemetry and optionally truncate/transform function payloads.
Jen: Console & billing implications: show a clear UI marker on requests that fell back + estimated extra tokens billed. Also a per-customer toggle to opt into relaxed fallbacks vs strict (for reliability vs cost).
Alex: Router config prototype (YAML) — this is what I had in mind: ```yaml
routing_policies:
  - name: eu-tiered-fallback
    tiers: [hosted, dedicated]
    fallback_order:
      - model: redwood/lg-quant
        require:
          tokenizer_hash: 9f8a
          tool_calling_schema_version: 2
      - model: redwood/lg-8bit
        allow_if:
          fallback_safety: relaxed
    telemetry: emit_on_fallback: true
```
Maria: Telemetry needs fields: `fallback_reason`, `original_model`, `final_model`, `tokens_original`, `tokens_final`, `broken_functions_count`, `region`, `customer_tier`. That will let us compute unit-cost delta and regression alerts.
Sam: For tool-calling parity tests I'll add a small harness that runs the canonical function-calling suite against model variants and reports diffs. Output = list of mismatched signatures + sample failing payloads.
Jen: Also add quota accounting rule: if tokens_final > tokens_original then router should optionally deduct delta from the customer quota or annotate invoice. Need product input but at least surface in UI.
Alex: UX note: in traces show inline banner: "fallbacked to redwood/lg-8bit — tool-calling may be degraded" with a one-click link to compatibility matrix row and telemetry. :warning:
deploy-bot: Canary job started for `router-fallback-specs` (canary=5%, regions=[eu-west, us-east]). Will auto-rollback if `fallback_safety: strict` checks fail.
Maria: I'll own the compat schema + telemetry mapping. Will open PR to compat-service and add `tokenizer_hash` + `tool_calling_schema_version` fields.
Sam: I'll add the function-calling CI checks and a test matrix that runs nightly across variants.
Jen: I'll draft console mockups for the per-customer fallback toggle and the trace banner.
Alex: Great — plan: PRs by EOD Wednesday, then small canary. Keep discussion here for any edge cases. Thanks! :thumbsup:
